attributes.title: Level 10

subgroups.name: Discover

steps.text: Watch this video to learn about changing image pixel colors, creating mini maps, using timers to control game flow and toggling between 2D and 3D game experience with the Raycasting extension!

questions.hint: What can the parameters tell you about how the function might be used?
questions.title: [Match one per answer] Match each function with its definition:

statements.text: The function takes 2 parameters: x and y. The parameters get the pixel color at the x and y-positions of the image.
The function takes 3 parameters: x, y, and color. The x and y parameters set the pixel’s position. The color parameter sets the pixel color.
The function takes 2 parameters: from and to. The from parameter is the color number of the pixels to change. The to parameter is the color number that the pixels will change to.

questions.correctResponse: Notice the setPixel and replace functions both make changes to a pixel, but the setPixel function can only change one pixel at a time while the replace function can change a group of pixels the same color (similarly to the image editor’s bucket tool)!

questions.hint: The Minimap is created as a sprite. Do sprite images automatically update?
questions.title: [Select one] When using the Minimap extension, the Minimap does not need to be continuously updated after it is created to provide accurate game information.
questions.correctResponse: The Minimap must be regularly updated to provide an accurate picture of the game to the user!

questions.hint: The throttle function takes 2 parameters: key, such as “action” and time.
questions.title: [Select one] The throttle function…

answers.text: Is a mechanism that regulates the flow of a fluid to control an engine’s power or speed.
Uniformly increases a projectile's velocity over the distance it travels until the projectile is destroyed.
Delays a repeated action in a game until a certain amount of time has passed.
Increases how often a repeated action in a game happens.

questions.correctResponse: The throttle function might be used to delay how frequently a Player sprite can send projectiles.

questions.hint: How might a “flat” floor or sky be created when using the Raycast extension?
questions.title: [Select one] When using the Raycast extension, all “colored tiles” in the tilemap become 3D walls for the player to navigate.
questions.correctResponse: Use a colored background image instead of tiles to create a “flat” floor or sky!

attributes.description: You’ve reached Level 10 of Brown Belt! Before you create your final Brown Belt project, there are a few neat tricks to learn that could take your game to the next level! Here are the achievements you’ll unlock in Level 10:

badges.title: Extension Explorer
badges.description: Use the minimap, status bar, timer, and raycasting extensions to enhance a project.

badges.title: Bird’s Eye View
badges.description: Create and pin a minimap displaying a smaller representation of sprites and the tilemap in a corner of the screen.

badges.title: Gauging the Action
badges.description: Make something happen based on the value of a status bar.

badges.title: Wait for the Signal
badges.description: Use throttle to delay an action in a game.

badges.title: Right on Cue
badges.description: Run a chunk of code after a certain amount of time has passed.

badges.title: In-Depth Image
badges.description: Create a 3D version of a tilemap from a sprite’s perspective.

badges.title: Points of View
badges.description: Toggle between 3D and top-down views of a tilemap.
